description.p: Skribisto is a writing app for novels, from the first idea to the finished manuscript.
Skribisto est un logiciel d'écriture pour les romans, de la première idée au manuscrit terminé.

ul.li: Split panes and tabs, and a whole chapter, part or book readable as one text
Écran partagé et onglets, et un chapitre, une partie ou le livre entier à lire comme un seul texte
Corkboard, story bible, margin comments and footnotes
Tableau de liège, bible narrative, commentaires dans la marge et notes de bas de page
Word goals, writing sessions, pace planning and manuscript analysis
Objectifs de mots, sessions d'écriture, planification du rythme et analyse du manuscrit
Statuses you name yourself, from first draft to final
Des statuts que vous nommez vous-même, du premier jet à la version finale
Import from Scrivener, Manuskript, Plume Creator, Word, OpenDocument or Markdown, comments included, with a report of anything left behind
Import depuis Scrivener, Manuskript, Plume Creator, Word, OpenDocument ou Markdown, commentaires compris, avec un rapport de ce qui n'a pas pu être repris
Export to DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF and more, and finish the page layout in the program you prefer
Export en DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF et d'autres formats, pour finir la mise en page dans le logiciel de votre choix
Search and replace, autosave, backups and version history
Rechercher et remplacer, enregistrement automatique, sauvegardes et historique des versions
Spell checking, smart punctuation and 24 interface languages
Correcteur orthographique, ponctuation intelligente et interface en 24 langues
Built for accessibility: screen readers, braille displays and keyboard shortcuts
Pensé pour l'accessibilité : lecteurs d'écran, plages braille et raccourcis clavier

ul.li: Everything but what you are writing can now fade back. Press F8, click the new button beside the spell-check one at the top right, or choose View ▸ Fade the rest of the text. In Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Focus you choose whether the sentence or the whole paragraph you are in keeps its full strength, and how far the rest fades: Light, Medium or Strong. In Full Chapter, Full Part and Full Book the other scenes fade as well, and so does the synopsis while you write the text below it. It works in distraction-free mode too, where the strip at the bottom has its own button, and it combines with Highlight around the caret and with typewriter scrolling

Paragraphs can now be justified. Justify sits beside Align left and Center in the Format panel and in Format ▸ Alignment. A justified paragraph stays justified in DOCX, ODT, EPUB, HTML and PDF exports, even when the export style sets the book ragged, so you can justify one passage, such as a letter, without justifying the whole book

Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Scene, Synopsis and Notes each have a new switch, Start justified. When you start writing in an empty text of that kind, its paragraph is justified, and so is each paragraph you add after it with Enter. Texts that already hold words keep their alignment, and Undo right after the first letter takes the justification off
The lists that open from Convert to…, Add to cast…, Set point of view…, File under a book… and Link to a note… now sit in a single frame. They used to show a frame inside a second, wider one

A DOCX export whose style justifies the text now marks its paragraphs justified the way Word reads it. The file used a value outside the DOCX standard, which word processors could ignore and show the text ragged

In the Resources panel, a folder's Resources page and Settings ▸ Work ▸ Resources, each file now shows its extension on a small coloured tag beside its size, such as pdf or docx. A title is the file's name without its extension, so two files called Map looked alike but for their icon. The colour comes from the extension: a PDF is red, a Word document blue, and files of the same type always share theirs

Scenes and chapters no longer share an icon shape. A scene now shows the three marks that separate scenes in a printed book, * * *, above two lines of text, and a chapter shows a page whose top is filled in, like the title area of a chapter's first page. They used to be the same page with a small difference inside it, which was hard to tell apart in the editor tabs. The new icons appear in the binder, the editor tabs, the corkboard, the Overview, the Search panel, the Trash, Go to, the destination pickers and Export

Renaming a chapter or a part that had no title now shows the new title in Full Part, Full Book and Full Synopsis straight away. These pages kept the name Skribisto gives an untitled chapter, such as Chapter 3, and switching to another page and back did not always bring the new title. Clearing a title now shows that name again instead of an empty heading

Add new chapter, at the end of Full Part and Full Book, now adds a chapter after the last one. It used to add a scene to the last chapter, in a window titled New scene. The windows that Add new chapter, Add new scene, Insert chapter and Insert scene open, on the corkboard too, now carry the name of the button you clicked. Clicking OK with no name now adds the item anyway: a chapter then has no title of its own and is numbered like any other, and a scene is called New scene. It used to do nothing, as if you had clicked Cancel

On the corkboard, Insert on a note card now reads Insert note, on a front or back matter card Insert paratext, and on the end of a book Insert book. It said Insert scene on every card that was not a chapter, whatever it then added

Full Synopsis now always shows the synopses. After turning on Read as exported in Full Book, Full Part or Full Chapter, switching to Full Synopsis used to show the exported text instead, with no switch on that page to turn it off. Read as exported stays on and applies again when you switch back

In the margin marks, the dialogue texture now follows the text when its lines wrap differently, after the window is resized for example. A paragraph's bar could stay a line away from its paragraph until the next edit to that scene

Full Book, Full Part, Full Chapter and Full Synopsis now show their outline: each chapter sits further in than its part, and each scene further in than its chapter. Choose how far in Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Page layout ▸ Indent by level, from None to Large. With a screen reader, each title is a heading one level below the one it belongs to

Full Book and Full Part, and their Full Synopsis, can now show only their outline: choose Show down to chapters or Show parts only above the text. A banner says what is hidden, and adding, moving, merging and splitting wait until everything is shown again. Each tab remembers its choice

Turning Read as exported on or off at the top of Full Book, Full Part or Full Chapter now leaves the page where it was. It used to scroll down to the first part, chapter or scene, out of sight of the switch you had just used

Help ▸ Report a Translation Error… has a new button, Continue on Discord, for writers without a GitHub account. It copies your report and opens the project’s translation channel on Discord, where you paste it into a message. The text under What will be public now offers it, and so does the help page

Right-clicking a scene, chapter or any other item in the binder now offers Set label, as the corkboard and Full Chapter already did. Right-click one of several selected items to label them all at once; one Undo then gives each back the label it had. Leave the field empty to remove a label
After changing a label, in the binder, on the corkboard, in Full Chapter or in the Overview, Edit ▸ Undo now reads Undo changing the label. It used to read Undo renaming
In Danish, Nummerér ikke dette kapitel in the binder's right-click menu now has U as its access key. It shared I with Importér her…, so the key could not reach both

Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Editor Behavior had grown too long and is now four pages. Page layout holds the text width, Indent by level, and where the synopsis and the epigraphs go. Focus holds typewriter scrolling, Highlight around the caret and Fade the rest of the text. Images & files holds what happens to large images you insert and to files over 10 MB you attach. Tabs kept open and Remember the last view for each item type are on a new page, Appearance & Behavior ▸ Tabs & views. Every setting keeps its value
Settings now opens on the page you were on last, instead of always on Appearance. A message that offers to open one page of Settings, and Help ▸ Keyboard shortcuts, still open on their own page

Undoing a move, a merge, a split or a duplicate in the binder now keeps the words you typed after it into a text that was still empty, such as a chapter's own text, a synopsis or an epigraph. The undo used to remove that text along with what it undid

In Search, the matches found in comments now start unticked for Replace All, as the Comments switch says. They started ticked whenever the search had just been run, so a Replace All changed your comments too unless you unticked each one

In Search, Replace this on a match you have not ticked, such as one in a comment, now replaces it. It used to change nothing and say nothing. And the question Replace All asks now counts only the matches it will change, not the unticked ones

In the Versions panel, Restore this version now refuses an item in the trash, whose text cannot be changed anywhere else: restore the item from the trash first. It used to rewrite the text of the trashed item

Every item that holds text now has a scratchpad, a page of private notes kept beside its text, for a question to settle, a fact to check or a list of changes for the next draft. Open it on the right of the window with its icon or Ctrl+Shift+A, or from View ▸ Panels. It shows the scratchpad of the item in front of you, and in Full Book, Full Part, Full Chapter and Full Synopsis that of the scene your cursor was in last. A scratchpad is saved and backed up with the project, but never exported, never counted in your words, targets or pace, and left out of Search unless you turn on the new Scratchpads switch among its options. With it on, their matches are listed unticked, as comments are, Replace All changes the ones you tick, and opening one selects it in the scratchpad. An item in the trash keeps its scratchpad, read-only, and merging two scenes joins theirs. Its earlier versions are in the Versions panel: choose Scratchpad at its top to compare them or put one back. Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Typography ▸ Scratchpad, a new page, sets its font and text size apart from those of your notes, and Ctrl+= in a scratchpad resizes only scratchpads

Importing from Scrivener, Manuskript or Plume Creator now puts the notes of each document, scene, chapter or folder into that item's own scratchpad. They used to arrive as a separate note titled with the item's name and (notes), placed next to it in the binder. Scrivener notes holding footnotes or comments, which a scratchpad cannot show, still arrive as that note, and the import says so. In Manuskript notes, the names of characters, world entries, plots and other items are written out as before, but no longer linked: the import says how many items this concerns
